name.en: Kami-shiho-gatame escape by action and reaction

about.en: A hold from above your head is hard to bridge straight out of, so you use their own correction against them: push one way, let them resist, then go the other. The syllabuses call it action and reaction, and it is the first escape that is about timing rather than strength.

en: Make the first movement real, or they will not react to it
Change direction the instant you feel them push back
Small, sharp movements beat one big heave
You are held in Kami-shiho-gatame, their chest on yours from above your head and their hands gripping your belt.
Bring both elbows in tight and place your hands on their hips or shoulders.
Push firmly to one side, turning your hips that way as though escaping in that direction.
Feel them brace and push back the other way to stop you: that is the reaction you wanted.
The instant you feel it, stop pushing and turn sharply the opposite way, adding your movement to theirs.
Turn onto your front or onto your knees as the space opens, and come up facing them.

receiving.en: Do not chase the first movement. If you feel them push, meet it with weight rather than with a shove of your own, and keep your hips low and wide: the escape only works if you overcommit to the correction.

viNotes.en: This escape suits touch better than sight, because the whole thing is a conversation through contact. Push, wait to feel the answer come back, then change direction. The timing cue arrives through your hands, never through your eyes.
